title: Minimum Garden Perimeter to Collect Enough Apples
summary: Given an integer neededApples, determine the smallest perimeter of a square plot centered at (0, 0) such that the plot contains at least the specified number of apples.
statement: Given an integer neededApples, determine the smallest perimeter of a square plot centered at (0, 0) such that the plot contains at least the specified number of apples. Each apple tree at coordinate (i, j) produces |i| + |j| apples.
constraints: The square is centered at the origin with corners (r,r), (r,-r), (-r,r), and (-r,-r).
A tree at integer coordinate (x,y) produces abs(x)+abs(y) apples; return the smallest perimeter 8r meeting the target.
hints: The total apples inside radius r is 2*r*(r+1)*(2*r+1), which increases monotonically.
Binary-search the smallest integer radius whose closed-form total reaches needed_apples, then multiply the side length 2r by four.
Double an upper radius until feasible; lower-bound search on apples(r)>=target; return 8*r.
Summing each newly added square ring gives 12r^2 and summing rings yields the formula. Monotonicity makes lower-bound binary search return the unique minimum radius.
